H1.note: title: elevated C4A/C4B dosage and C1q-initiated tagging raise risk, CSMD1 loss removes the brake (so CSMD1 is neg). C4B is named only in the title and gene list; no step mentions it. The chain breaks after H1.1 (C4 protein, then C1QA) and after H1.2/H1.3 (classical complement cascade, then complement tagging of synapses), so no gene reaches schizophrenia.

H2.note: title: loss of tonic C1q/CX3CR1 surveillance causes the disease, so both are neg. C4A/C4B are in the gene list, and the mechanism says C4 lowers microglia-synapse contact, but no overall direction is stated for them, so no claim. The C1QA steps end at mouse current phenotypes (H2.1) and first-episode psychosis (H2.2), not schizophrenia.

H3.note: NXPH3's sign comes from the mechanism (its knockout gives schizophrenia-relevant endophenotypes); the step to schizophrenia (H3.3) is unsigned and starts at a different node, so the chain effectively ends at the startle / gating phenotypes, hence the two phenotype claims. CCDC136 is claimed to be a passenger with no effect: BioLean has no claim form for that, so no claim.

H4.note: title: liver-derived C4 drives the association (C4 = C4A and C4B; the mechanism names both as hepatic). CX3CR1's sign is from the mechanism ('microglia as the effector reading the imported signal', H4.3 required_for, and the druggable-target framing); it is not stated outright. C1QA is in the gene list with no direction.

findings.detail: H1.1 ends at 'C4 protein at synapse' and H1.2 starts at C1QA; no step links C4 to the classical cascade, so neither C4A nor C4B has a route.

H1.2 and H1.3 end at 'classical complement cascade' (GO:0006958) and H1.4 starts at 'complement tagging of synapses' (opsonization at synapses, GO:0008228); different nodes, and no step or cited text links them, so C1QA and CSMD1 never reach pruning or schizophrenia.
H1's title is about 'elevated C4A/C4B dosage' but C4B appears in no step; the same holds for H4 ('liver-derived C4').

H1 is rated 'high' although its chain breaks twice, H1.5 (pruning causes schizophrenia) has no supporting citation, and the contradicting papers it lists (PMID:38301948 lower C1q; PMID:41903141 C4 overexpression reduces spine elimination) cut directly against it.

rs116633139 is a GWAS row for 'Autism spectrum disorder or schizophrenia' with risk allele '?', intergenic near HLA-DQB1; the mechanism presents it as a schizophrenia C4 signal (OR~1.16), and it says nothing about C4 protein amount.

Both H1.2 citations are gene-set enrichment results (Reactome 'Initial triggering of complement', STRING GO:0006958); the step is stated only by the run's own H2.2 citation PMID:38301948 ('the C1q initiated classical activation axis'), moved here.
UniProt Q96PZ7's function text is 'Potential suppressor of squamous cell carcinomas'; the run reads its Sushi domain list as complement inhibition. PMID:40112933 does state the step (in vitro).
PMID:35396580 (PGC 2022) implicates synaptic organization and transmission broadly; it names no complement, pruning, cortical thinning or neurexin (the run's H3.3 note admits the last).

PMID:41903141, cited by H2.4 and listed as contradicting by H1 and H4, says C4 overexpression reduces spine elimination, 'contrary to the models of excessive microglia-mediated synaptic elimination'; attached to H1.4 as refuting.

H1.5 (excess pruning causes schizophrenia) cites only PMID:26814963, which says complement activity 'may help explain the reduced numbers of synapses' in schizophrenia brains: a disease feature, not a cause.

H1's contradicting entry 'AGR:MGI:88228 C4b-null mice show only immune/kidney phenotypes, no synaptic or behavioural phenotype' is prose with an accession inside; no record was fetched, so it cannot be checked.

The run's own citations state the C4-schizophrenia link that H1 and H4 rest on (PMID:26814963 'each common C4 allele associating with schizophrenia in proportion to its tendency to generate greater expression of C4A'; PMID:42276261 'SZ was associated with C4 overexpression'), but no step states it, so it cannot carry either hypothesis.

H2's four steps share no nodes: H2.1 ends at mouse postsynaptic-current phenotypes, H2.2 is a separate C1q association with first-episode psychosis, H2.3 ends at microglial synaptic surveillance and H2.4 starts at degraded microglial synaptic refinement; the mechanism's 'surveillance/refinement' treats two processes as one.

H2.2's object is first-episode psychosis, broader than schizophrenia (66 of 113 later diagnosed), although the same paper reports lower C1QA mRNA in schizophrenia prefrontal cortex and concludes C1q is lower in schizophrenia; the run also set polarity 'unknown' while its note gives the decrease.

None of H2.3's citations states that CX3CR1 is needed for microglial surveillance: HPA is an expression level, PMID:22632727 is about CR3/C3, PMID:42276261 about CX3CR1 expression. The nearest support, UniProt text inside OT:CX3CR1-tractability ('participating in synaptic pruning', By similarity), sits at no step.
H2.4 (degraded refinement causes schizophrenia) and H4.3 (CX3CR1 needed for the response to opsonised synapses) keep no citation; H4.3's STRING edge is text-mining only, as the run's note admits.

PMID:41903141 states that C4 overexpression lowers microglial surveilled volume and synapse contacts in mouse cortex, the one link H2's mechanism leans on for C4, but no H2 step expresses C4 to surveillance.
H2's mechanism says C1qa-null mice show absence seizures; none of the cited MGI records (currents, bouton morphology) reports seizures.

H1 claims C1QA raises risk and excess pruning causes schizophrenia; H2 claims C1QA loss and degraded refinement cause it. The run offers both as alternatives, yet rates H1 'high' while listing H2's key evidence (lower C1q) against it.

The Nxph3 knockout records report increased startle reflex and abnormal spatial learning; none reports prepulse inhibition or sensorimotor gating, which the run equates with startle. The step's context (cortical excitatory neurons) is also not what a global knockout tests.

NXPH3's steps end at startle and gating phenotypes; the step to schizophrenia (H3.3) starts at 'altered neurexin-complex signalling', is unsigned and has no citation naming neurexins, and GWAS reports no NXPH3 association.
H3's mechanism says 'CSMD1-null mice show the mirror-image decreased startle'; no CSMD1 mouse record is among the sources.

H3 calls NXPH3 'expressed in brain excitatory neurons', but its HPA record (cited as supporting) shows higher expression in blood vessel and smooth muscle cells (29.8 nCPM) than brain excitatory neurons (6.6 nCPM).

H3.4 encodes an explicit negative ('no GWAS association', CCDC136 a passenger) as 'associated_with' with polarity unknown, and the same record GWAS:CCDC136:no-association is cited both as chain evidence and as contradicting evidence for H3.

H4's premise 'HPA finds C4A and C4B predominantly hepatic and adrenal with minimal brain detection' has no source: the cited HPA:ENSG00000173372 is C1QA's record, and no C4A or C4B HPA record was fetched.

H4 lists PMID:26814963 as contradicting, and it reports C4A and C4B expression in the brain and C4 protein at synapses, refuting H4's 'minimal brain detection' premise outright; H4 was kept anyway (confidence low).

H4 casts CX3CR1 as the microglial effector of a risk signal (pos), but its own H4.4 citation PMID:42276261 reports CX3CR1 underexpression in schizophrenia, so the only arm (via H4.4) has the opposite sign; the same arm agrees with H2.
rs12541020 (T allele, OR 1.061 for schizophrenia, author gene CSMD1) is signed but no step states a CSMD1 association; the mechanism's 'p=6e-9' matches.
OT:CSMD1-MONDO_0005090 (score 0.51, genetic 0.81) supports no step; Open Targets scores carry no direction.
R-HSA-174577 ('Activation of C3 and C5') and R-HSA-977606 ('Regulation of Complement cascade') are enrichment results at no step.
STRING:C1QA-C4A (database 0.90) would suit a binds step, but the run has none for C1QA and C4A.
PMID:39616737 states no step; it finds C1QA mRNA increased in high-inflammation schizophrenia subependymal zone, which sits awkwardly with H2's 'C1q is lower'.
AGR:MGI:88223:MP:0008571 (C1qa knockout, abnormal synaptic bouton morphology) and HPA:ENSG00000173372 (C1QA expression) support no step of H2.
AGR:MGI:1336188:MP:0001392 (Nxph3 knockout, abnormal locomotor behavior) and HPA:ENSG00000182575 (NXPH3 expression) support no step.

R-HSA-9968734 ('Differentiation of Circulating Monocytes' enrichment), OT:CX3CR1-tractability (druggability) and OT:C4A-MONDO_0005090 (score 0.09, literature only) support no step; the last undercuts 'C4 is the strongest complement signal'.
BLN:AlphaNeurexin: no ontology term for the alpha-neurexin class (PR has only single isoforms such as neurexin-1-alpha PR:000029250).
BLN:MicroglialSynapticSurveillance: GO has no process for microglia monitoring or contacting synapses, though PMID:41903141 measures it ('microglial surveilled volume').
BLN:MicroglialSynapticRefinement: GO has synapse pruning (GO:0098883) but nothing for the accuracy or timing of pruning, which is what H2 claims is degraded.

No MONDO or HP term for first-episode psychosis; grounded as psychotic disorder (MONDO:0005485), dropping 'first episode'. MONDO:0005485 also lists 'mental or behavioral disorder' as a synonym, which is wrong.

No form for an absent association ('CCDC136 is not associated with schizophrenia') or for a hypothesis claim that a gene is a passenger with no effect; assoc direction 'none' means unsigned, not absent.

Steps where a gene raises its own product at a place ('C4 protein at synapse', 'circulating C4 protein') were split into a location rel plus a not_causal entry; the guide covers neither the location nor the split for this case.
The run's relation 'translocates' is not in the guide's relation table; it could be an effect between C4A refined to blood and to CSF, but the guide does not say.

'Required for normal X' was written as the gene lowering the MP 'abnormal X' phenotype (sign neg, with a sign_note); the guide covers 'abnormal X' for undirected objects but not 'required for normal X', so another curator may write it differently.

The guide allows a bridge that 'a text the run cited states', but does not say whether a cited gene-disease association (C4A or C1QA with schizophrenia) may bridge straight past a broken chain; I added none, so H1's C4A claim and H2's C1QA claim have no route even though cited texts state those associations.

Cortical thinning was grounded to UPHENO:0080827 'decreased thickness of the cerebral cortex': HP has only atrophy, MP is mouse-only, and the guide's phenotype row does not list UPHENO although render.py accepts it.
A GWAS Catalog 'no association among curated associations' lookup is absence of a catalogued hit, not a tested null; recording it as observational evidence overstates it.

The run's only 'established' arm (NXPH3 lowering abnormal startle reflex, belief 4/5) rests on one MGI mouse knockout annotation: the statement row says taxonConsistent false, but the belief and verdict take no account of it.

PMID:41903141's refuting span summarises the authors' own earlier in vivo mouse work ('our previous results indicate'); by the guide that is a background sentence (review), though the design behind it is mechanistic.
PMID:22632727's abstract does not name the species (it is a mouse study); I set taxon mouse from knowledge of the paper, which the guide neither allows nor forbids.

A contradicting citation can refute a hypothesis's premise (PMID:26814963 against H4's 'minimal brain C4') when no statement carries that premise; it then has nowhere to attach as refuting and can only be excluded.

Every contradicting citation in this run is also cited in a chain or as supporting, so sources.json marks none 'contradicting'; they can be found only in run.json, and one ('AGR:MGI:88228 ...') is prose with no record.

The run gives structured step contexts (astrocyte, microglia, hippocampus, cortical excitatory neuron, cerebral cortex, liver). I dropped them as places rather than limits, except liver for H4 where the place is the point; the guide's 'context limits the result' test is unclear for a structured context field.
